title: Cleaning toilets, wash basins, urinals and washrooms
audience: Trained cleaners and supervisors who clean toilets, wash basins, urinals and washroom furniture in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Set up a washroom safely with a cleaning-in-progress sign, ventilation and colour-coded equipment.
Protect yourself from infection by covering cuts, wearing gloves throughout and washing hands at the end.
Clean in the order dirty areas first, then clean areas, with washroom cloths and brushes kept for washroom use only.
Remove chewing gum and waste from urinals and toilets before cleaning them.
Restock consumables, report faulty fixtures and judge the finished washroom against the stated standard.

instruction.heading: Why washrooms need the strictest routine
instruction.body: Washrooms carry some of the highest concentrations of germs in most buildings, and cleaners work close to them. The rule in the source is that equipment and materials used here are never used outside the washroom. That rule stops germs moving into kitchens and office surfaces. The task also happens in a space that customers may be using, so the cleaner must be courteous, careful and visible. The source names a hygiene areas standard from the British Institute of Cleaning Sciences framework.

instruction.heading: Setting up and protecting yourself
instruction.body: Put a cleaning-in-progress sign on the door so that customers know the washroom is being serviced. Where the washroom is shared, follow your workplace rules on who may enter and when. Check your hands for open cuts before you put gloves on, and cover any cut with a waterproof plaster. Gloves are worn for the whole task. Eye protection is used when splash or spray is possible. Open windows or doors where possible, and make sure no chemical fumes are present in the area while you work.

instruction.heading: The cleaning order
instruction.body: Turn off the urinal water supply if you can. Empty all bins, and use a litter picker to remove chewing gum and waste from the urinals. Flush the toilet with the lid down to reduce splash, and push the water past the U-bend with the brush. Apply toilet cleaner to the urinal and the toilet. Disinfect the dirty areas first: the door locks, the toilet roll holder, the base and flush of the toilet, the tiles around it, the cistern, the seat and lid, and the brush holder. Then do the outside of the urinal, its tiles and the floor around it. Clean the clean areas next, from the sink, taps and tiles to the soap dispenser, the dryer or towel dispenser, and the exit handle. Use the cloth colour your business has assigned to washroom clean-up areas, and rinse the cloth often. Use a separate colour for the toilet and urinal rinse work, and never use either set outside the washroom. Scrub the inside of the toilet with the toilet brush, flush with the lid down, and scrub the urinal with the brush or a scouring pad before rinsing it.

instruction.heading: Finishing the washroom
instruction.body: Turn the urinal water back on. Restock toilet roll, soap and paper towels. Clean the mirrors. Mop the floor using the single-solution method in “Single-solution wet mopping”. Take off your gloves, wash your hands, and replace any plaster you are wearing. Report any broken seat, fixture or fitting. Remove waste according to the customer's disposal guidelines. Do not leave any product within reach of a customer.

instruction.heading: The washroom standard
instruction.body: A finished washroom meets the following standard. Walls, doors and cubicle partitions are washed with a disinfectant on a regular schedule. Towel holders and dispensers are clean, dry and free of dust and marks, with clean towels fitted. The outside of hand dryers is clean, dry and free of smears. Sanitary ware, including sinks, basins, baths, WC bowls, seats, covers, taps, outlets, plugs, urinals, brushes, toilet roll holders and tiled surfaces, is free of scum, grease, hair, scale, dust, soil, spillage and removable stains. Soap dispensers are filled, working, with clean nozzles and clean external surfaces, and bar soap is replaced when needed. Supplies are stocked at all times. Mirrors are free of smears.

procedure: Put up the cleaning-in-progress sign. Check the workplace rules for who may enter and when.
Check your hands for cuts and cover any cut with a waterproof plaster. Put on gloves, and eye protection where splash is possible.
Ventilate the room, check that no chemical fumes are present, and turn off the urinal water if you can.
Empty the bins. Use a litter picker to remove chewing gum and waste from the urinals.
Flush the toilet with the lid down, push the water past the U-bend, and apply toilet cleaner to the urinal and toilet.
Disinfect the dirty areas first, then the outside of the urinal and the floor around it.
Wipe the clean areas from the sink to the exit handle with the designated cloth, rinsing it often.

Scrub the toilet and urinal interiors with their designated brushes, flush with the lid down, and rinse. Turn the urinal water back on, restock consumables, clean the mirrors, and mop the floor by the “Single-solution wet mopping” method.
Remove gloves, wash your hands, replace any plaster, report faults, remove waste, and return the colour-coded equipment to storage.

workedExamples.situation: Partway through a washroom you notice a cut on your finger that was not covered before you started.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop before the next task. Remove and dispose of the gloves, wash the hand, cover the cut with a waterproof plaster, and put on new gloves. Do not continue with exposed or inadequately protected skin. If the cut broke the skin during the job, record it under the workplace incident procedure.

workedExamples.situation: A toilet bowl is blocked, and the water level is rising during your clean.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Do not keep flushing or force the water down. Keep the lid down, keep customers out of the area, and report the blockage to your supervisor. Clearing a blockage is not part of this lesson. Keep the cleaning products away from the area until the situation has been assessed.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves, worn for the whole task.
Eye protection where splash or spray is possible.
Washroom-only colour-coded set: cloths, buckets, brushes, gloves and litter picker, kept for washroom use.
Toilet brush and urinal scrubbing pad.
Toilet cleaner and disinfectant approved for the surfaces.
Consumables: toilet roll, soap, paper towels and dispensers.
Litter picker for gum and waste.

commonErrors.error: Using washroom cloths or buckets in a kitchen or office.
commonErrors.prevention: Washroom equipment stays in the washroom and is stored separately by colour.
Cover the cut before gloves go on, and check again each time gloves are changed.

commonErrors.error: Flushing with the lid up, so that splash spreads.
Cleaning clean areas before the dirty ones.
commonErrors.prevention: Dirty areas first, then clean areas.

commonErrors.error: Leaving products within reach of customers.
commonErrors.prevention: Never leave products unattended in the washroom. Store them away when you step out.
Restock as one of the final steps before you leave.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Infection control: wear gloves throughout, cover open cuts, and wash your hands at the end. The source links this to the risk of infectious disease.
Chemicals follow “Chemical competency: reading labels and safety data sheets”: check the SDS and label, never mix products, and keep no chemical fumes in the area while cleaning.
Hygiene standard: the source names a hygiene areas standard from the British Institute of Cleaning Sciences framework. The name is referenced only.
Shared washrooms: follow the workplace rules on who may enter and when, and treat customers using the facility with courtesy.

Sharps or body fluids found in a washroom are outside this routine. Stop, keep people away, and follow the sharps and body fluid procedure for your business. This lesson does not authorise handling of those materials.

qualityStandard: Walls, doors and cubicle partitions washed with disinfectant on the scheduled routine.
Sanitary ware, taps, seats and urinals free of scum, grease, hair, scale, dust, soil, spillage and removable stains.
Towel holders clean, dry and free of marks, with clean towels fitted.
Soap dispensers filled, working, with clean nozzles; bar soap replaced when needed.
Mirrors free of smears, and consumables restocked before leaving.
documentationEvidence: Washroom clean record with the time and the checks completed.
Defect report for any fixture or fitting, with its location.
Record of any cut or exposure, with the first aid given and who was told.
summary: Washroom equipment is used only in the washroom and stored by colour.
Cover cuts before gloves go on, and wash your hands at the end.
Dirty areas first, then clean areas; lid down on every flush.
Finish by restocking, reporting faults and checking the washroom against the standard.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before you put on gloves in a washroom, what must you check?
options: Nothing, because gloves protect the hands from cuts on their own
Your hands for open cuts, and cover any cut with a waterproof plaster first
That the colour of the gloves matches the sink and the bin lid colour

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct order for disinfecting a washroom?
options: Clean areas first, then the toilet
Start at the mirror and finish at the toilet
Dirty areas first, then clean areas

knowledgeChecks.question: Where are washroom cloths and brushes used?
options: Only in the washroom, and stored separately by colour
In the kitchen, if the kitchen is also being cleaned
On office desks, once the washroom is finished
